scenes.title: The discovery club
scenes.caption: The message says use this code to sign in. A second sender calls it a prize ticket and asks Kabir to forward it. Meera reads the original purpose instead of accepting the label supplied by the person asking for it.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A problem to solve
scenes.caption: Some codes identify public events, while other codes approve access or actions. The word code alone cannot establish what is shareable. A login or approval code is a secret; forwarding it may allow someone else to complete the action it authorises.
scenes.speech: Some codes identify public events, while other codes approve access or actions. The word code alone cannot establish what is shareable. A login or approval code is a secret; forwarding it may allow someone else to complete the action it authorises.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Try the idea
scenes.caption: The class uses labels instead of real numbers and never requests an actual one-time password. If a code arrives unexpectedly, students tell a trusted adult. If one was already shared, they seek help promptly rather than sending more codes or trusting a promise that the first request was harmless.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose and explain
scenes.caption: The original message says the code signs in to an account. A different sender claims it is needed for a prize. Compare the actions, then inspect the explanation before moving on.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: See the consequence
scenes.caption: Keep the sign-in code private and ask a trusted adult about the unexpected request. The original authorisation purpose matters more than the sender’s new nickname for the code.
scenes.speech: Keep the sign-in code private and ask a trusted adult about the unexpected request. The original authorisation purpose matters more than the sender’s new nickname for the code.
